decision: tools/release.sh ends with orfoni announce-release, and the hub sends released to each connected app that asked with watchReleases; the app looks for its update on that message and on every connection to the hub, and the six-hour timer is gone
why: he wanted the update offered as soon as it is out without polling; releases are only ever made on this server, and the hub already holds a connection to every app
evidence: hub, protocol, CLI, client and UpdateButton tests; live check through the real hub

decision: the hub sends released only to apps that asked for it
why: an app up to 0.3.21 refuses a hub message it does not know, as 0.3.20 refused the peer item
evidence: hub test: a client that did not ask gets nothing

decision: released carries the version but the app still checks latest.json and the installer's signature itself
why: the message is only a nudge, so a hub that is wrong or compromised cannot make the app install anything
evidence: the app calls the same updater check as at start

decision: not watching GitHub for releases from the hub
why: that is polling again, or a public webhook, for releases that only this server makes

decision: a Windows app offering an update as soon as release.sh announces it
why: needs the next release, since 0.3.21 neither asks nor knows the message

decision: each session's status line repeats the plan windows its Claude Code saw at its last reply, every 10 s: one round traced from the hub's socket had 14, 18, 34, 36 and 38% of the same 5-hour window and 13 to 17% of the same week, and some sessions only the weekly window
why: the status bar showed 14% and 13% while he saw 38% and 17%
evidence: strace of the hub's reads, 14 sessions

decision: the hub keeps each plan window apart: a later reset time replaces the window before, within one window the highest share wins, and a report without a window leaves it
why: a window's share only grows until it starts afresh, so the highest share of the latest window is the freshest; the app already hides a window whose reset has passed
evidence: hub test with an active and an idle session; live: the hub showed 39% and 17%, the highest the sessions reported
